payload.as_is:
INHERITS the resident as-is; these are the NEW pains, each with its witness from the record rather than from impression.

PAIN 1 - THE LANE CANNOT OPEN THE TWO DOCUMENTS THE PROCESS REQUIRES. se_file_read takes a path and nothing else, so se-v2-design.md (132k chars) is refused as too large and cannot be read at all through the lane; v1 sits outside the repo root and is unreachable by any se tool. Meanwhile the standing porting law requires consulting BOTH on every piece of porting work. WITNESS: three se_help misses on three separate days asking for exactly this - 2026-07-23 16:00 'read se-v2-design.md from the owner's working folder (outside the v2 root)', 2026-07-23 17:39 'read another repo v1 method files', 2026-07-24 07:28 'read v1 files method engage retro - declared-roots search scope is only planned for i3'. None was ever served. The contradiction is designed in: the process mandates reading sources the tools cannot open.

PAIN 2 - THE AGENT VOUCHES FOR ITS OWN CONFORMANCE IN PROSE. Gates ask the agent to assert models_adhered, red_observed, designs_realized, adrs_traced, verifiable, breaks_if_removed - every one of them a statement the agent writes about work the agent just did. WITNESS: i8d, where all ten gates were self-blessed under the owner's grant and the evidence was my own prose about my own build; the defects that shipped anyway were caught by the owner's thumb, not by any gate.

PAIN 3 - GUIDANCE DOES NOT REACH THE AGENT IT BINDS. Each packet carries one hand-written paragraph from its state node, with [[wikilinks]] left unresolved; applies_to matching is not performed. WITNESS: four laws were minted on 2026-07-25 - whitelist-guards, imports-are-read-only, workaround-then-record-the-gap, responsibility-never-delegates - each carrying an applies_to, and NONE of them will appear in any future packet. A session tomorrow can only learn them by accident.

PAIN 4 - THE MOST-USED TOOL IS THE MOST FRUSTRATING. se_file_patch applies exactly one edit per call while se_set_apply batches ledger ops freely. WITNESS: 645 calls, three times the next product tool, and 28 failures, more than any other - measured over the whole log, not felt. It produced a hand-rolled sweep script in i8d when six call sites needed the same change.

PAIN 5 - SEARCH ANSWERS THE WRONG QUESTION CONFIDENTLY, AND CANNOT SEE THE RECORD. se_file_search returns bare single lines with no context, no globs, no multiline; locating one line in engine/project.ts took four calls. It also coerces missing required args instead of refusing, so a wrong arg name searched the product for the literal word 'undefined' and returned real, correctly-formatted hits that answered nothing. And it sees only the working tree - since i5d withheld iteration evidence from trunk, no past iteration's evidence is searchable at all. WITNESS: 2026-07-25, the wrong search cost a wrong conclusion and a retracted note; the record blindness is structural, not yet witnessed only because nobody has needed to search a shipped iteration since i5d.

PAIN 6 - THE FENCE IS ENFORCED ON THE HONEST PATH AND OPEN ON THE OTHER. se-fence blocks Bash, Grep and Read against the product, but se_run executes arbitrary node, so a script edits product files with no CAS guard, no recorded diff and no ledger trace. WITNESS: ctor-sweep.mjs rewrote six product files during i8d with no record; the owner caught it in chat, not the system. The fence enumerated the tools that must not touch the product instead of naming the one way it may be touched.

PAIN 7 - THE MACHINE-LOCAL CONFIG HAS NO LANE AT ALL. ~/.se/<project>/*.json holds the pairing and now the brief store's credentials, and nothing on the surface reads, writes or validates it - not for the agent, not for the owner. WITNESS: enabling the brief store during i8d required a hand-rolled script; the owner, told this, asked 'why didn't you use the tools that we have?' - because they do not exist. The same absence makes a typo in that config indistinguishable from a deliberate opt-out.

PAIN 8 - THE RECORD DEPENDS ON A NAME ANYONE CAN DELETE. The close tags each iteration's evidence, but the tags are LIGHTWEIGHT, and push.followTags carries only annotated ones - so the config every VS Code user would set pushes the commits and silently drops every iter/* tag. The grant records evidence_tag, a name, and no commit hash. WITNESS: verified 2026-07-25 on iter/i8d-phone-brief - git rev-parse on the tag and on tag^{commit} return the identical hash, which is only true of a lightweight tag.
